content.title: Floodplain Risk
content.summary: Many homes in Arvada's floodplain were built before the floodplain regulations were established in 1974, particularly in neighborhoods along Ralston Creek. Property owners can check if their property is in a floodplain using the Interactive Floodplain Map and are encouraged to consider flood insurance due to the potential for significant damage from even a small amount of water. The Engineering Division offers assistance for assessing flooding risks and can provide site visits for property owners.
content.body:
## Know Your Risk

Most homes located in Arvada's floodplain were constructed before the floodplains officially existed. Arvada's floodplains took effect in 1974 and most of the neighborhoods along the creeks; including Ralston Creek, were already built.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=3066)

### Is my property in a floodplain?

Check the [Interactive Floodplain Map](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=6dea6f00d3f14106b3c8350de9b38a78) or contact the Engineering Division by [email](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#284d464f41464d4d5a41464f584d5a45415c5b68495a5e494c4906475a4f) or at 720-898-7640.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=3066)

### Do I need flood insurance?

Just a few inches of water can cause tens of thousands of dollars in property damage. Visit the [flood insurance page](/698).

## Need Assistance?

Engineering staff can meet with property owners to assess your flooding risk. If available, historic flooding and location-specific information will be provided. Site visits can assess flooding, drainage, and sewer problems and answer any related questions. Contact the Engineering Division by [email](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#e98c878e80878c8c9b80878e998c9b84809d9aa9889b9f888d88c7869b8e) or at 720-898-7640.
